p: בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (אֱמוֹר, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קד, א):
In the holy Zohar (Emor, Zohar III 104a):
״אָז תִּתְעַנַּג עַל ה׳״ וְגוֹ׳ (יְשַׁעְיָה נח, יד).
'Then you shall delight in Hashem,' etc." (Yeshayah 58:14).
(סוֹף פָּרָשַׁת אַחֲרֵי, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג עט, ב):
for children depend on the holy mazal, etc.;
and the upper tip of the yud
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (שָׁם סה, ב),
as stated in the holy Zohar (ibid. 65b);
of all hidden ones, which is called Ayin.
as stated in the holy Zohar
of the holy Atika shone forth
in His crowns, engraved and inscribed in the alef,
and the alef bored into the darkness
and shone to every side, etc.,
And it is stated in the holy Zohar
there is chessed and there is chessed, etc.;
the supernal chessed is 'above the heavens,' etc."
who merited recognizing the middah of Atika;
and this is what is said,
"And Avraham was old, coming with days" (Bereishis 24:1),
and it is stated in the holy Zohar
(חַיֵּי שָׂרָה, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קכט, א):
that is, he was refined in all the middos
and this is why it says 'old,' precisely.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא פז, א):
And this is what the Gemara says (Bava Metzia 87a):
"Until Avraham there was no old age";
that is, there was no one
(בְּרֵאשִׁית, זֹהַר חֵלֶק א כו, א, סוֹף עַמּוּד א);
(Bereishis, Zohar I 26a, end of the amud);
for on Sukkos one also merits
as stated in Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas
which is a day of the souls
and not a day of the body,
as stated in the holy Zohar
(וַיַּקְהֵל, זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רה, א, סוֹף עַמּוּד א).
(Vayakhel, Zohar II 205a, end of the amud).
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (סוּכָּה ב, א):
And as we have explained regarding what was taught (Sukkah 2a):
Now the phrase 'all seven days' is superfluous,
that the festival of Sukkos is seven days;
that in all the seven middos
and it is not written 'in six' —
one must leave the permanent dwelling
that is, to be like Shabbos,
which is a day of the souls
and not a day of the body at all,
as stated in the holy Zohar
And this is a dwelling for Hashem Yisbarach,
"And where is the place of My rest?" etc.;
"But to this one will I look,
to the poor and broken in spirit,
and this is expounded (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah)
as referring to the day of Shabbos.
And so on Sukkos the Torah said,
is called an 'inn' in the Gemara
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּגְּמָרָא מוֹעֵד קָטָן ט, ב);
(as written in the Gemara, Moed Katan 9b);
that it is a temporary dwelling,
then he becomes a dwelling for the Shechinah.
And this is what is said (Vayikra 23:43):
"So that your generations may know," etc.,
that this applies for all generations;
even after there will cease and be destroyed
the Beis HaMikdash and the Mishkan,
which are a dwelling for the Shechinah,
And this is what was said (Tanchuma Emor 22):
to make a sukkah for Me,
to repay Me My kindness, etc.,
as though you were doing kindness before Me, etc."
it likens the mitzvah of sukkah
to one who comes to pour a cup for his master.
And the point is: on Rosh Hashanah
there is the mitzvah of shofar,
so that they accept the yoke of His kingship
on Yom Kippur, the mitzvah of affliction;
and in a fast, the diminishing of my fat and blood
is as though I had offered it
"My offering, My bread for My fires."
And regarding sukkah, it is stated in the holy Zohar
קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חָדֵי עִמֵּיהּ וְכוּלֵּי;
Kudsha Brich Hu rejoices with him, etc."
pouring a cup for his master,
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
in the manner of what the holy Zohar says
is like pouring a cup for one's master.
